files.purpose: Common AuthorAttack entry point and original CLI defaults.
Bind original translation and target stages to shared role clients and temporary file storage; group physical source lines by repository example.
Shared configuration validation, source loading, request traces, OpenRouter transport, and explicit dispatch.
Common AuthorRunResult and AuthorStepResult conversion, retaining source-line records and raw versus file-formatted responses.

preserved_behavior: All nine language templates and target context examples retain exact original bytes.
Original physical-line input loading and stripping; more-than-13-token splitting gate; original splitter/extractor parsing, format retries, optional safety checks and phrase reversal.
Translation completes for the whole batch before target generation. Original phrase CSV serialization/reloading and language file assembly are executed.
Independent translator ALL and target SQL defaults; original single-language C++ missing output and delimiter mismatch (one residual hyphen for non-final records, four for the final record).
Original helper generation settings remain omitted. Target uses stream=false, max_tokens=512, temperature=0, top_p=1, seed=0 by default; source target CLI overrides remain available.
Original four-message target context and response newline escaping. No added post-run scoring, application retry limit, or local RNG seed.

Separator text inside extracted fields can produce additional target calls. These calls are retained; target_index identifies the target row and sentence_index identifies its original physical input line.

behavior.reference_execution: Independent subprocess executes complete official helper/template modules, translator.py main, and test.py main using native SDK serialization and real temporary files. It does not import the production source loader or binding. For attribution metadata only, the oracle re-executes the original pure assembler with a capture callback and locates its assembled strings in the actual file; production instead observes original write boundaries. Printed target output is captured before universal-newline normalization of saved file text.
compared: Prompt/context bytes and all nine language files
CSV phrase round trip, physical-line ownership, batch request order, delimiter artifacts, C++ missing file
Source request controls and omitted helper defaults; raw replies and escaped file output
Splitter/extractor retries; optional verification, phrase reversal, original NLTK assignment quirk
API errors, response-shape failures, SDK retries/delays, empty datasets, and common repository result serialization
Literal and JSON-escaped Unicode are kept distinct by the original regex parser
Delimiter-created target fragments retain source-line ownership; target carriage returns and newline escaping match original print/file behavior
allowed_comparison_differences: OpenRouter endpoint, model IDs, and provider routing fields
Repository example grouping, measured time, and temporary output paths
behavior.counting_note: The current suites comprise 305 prerequisite checks and 57 final QueryAttack checks. The 305 prerequisites passed in the combined regression run; only QueryAttack-specific code/tests changed afterward. The final 85-check run contains all 57 QueryAttack checks and repeats 28 verifier checks already included in the prerequisites. Counts overlap and are not summed. There was no single 362-check rerun after the final QueryAttack changes.

execution_requirements.baseline_python: QUERY_ATTACK_AUTHOR_PYTHON uses the environment.lock.txt baseline; QUERY_ATTACK_SHARED_PYTHON uses the shared SDK with NLTK. NLTK_DATA may select a common data directory.
execution_requirements.test_process: Intel macOS repository test process adds the Torch recompile_limit option as documented in docs/openrouter.md. All HTTP replies are scripted and in-memory.

verification_results.limitations: Exact source identity and scripted behavior comparisons do not establish identical live model responses, exhaustive SDK equivalence, attack effectiveness, or paper benchmark reproduction. Early NLTK resource validation and excluded post-run evaluation are documented departures. The author does not pin NLTK data revisions; historical tokenizer/tagger data equivalence is not established.

nltk_data.description: Both comparison environments and public integration tests use the same downloaded English resources. The author does not pin their historical data revision.
